title: Temporal Equivalence Principle: Synchronization Holonomy in Pulsar Scintillation
abstract:
The scalar-factorizable thin-screen delay model tested here assigns each scattered ray an additive scalar delay, so differential delays around a closed triplet cancel identically: τ_ij+τ_jk+τₖᵢ=0. The Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) instead predicts that proper-time transport is path-dependent in dilute, unscreened environments, producing a non-zero synchronization holonomy. This paper reports the rejection of the scalar-delay null hypothesis in pulsar scintillation using the phase-domain closure statistic ψ, a zero-centered circular observable that separates geometric phase from folded-noise bias.

The primary target is PSR J0437-4715, analyzed with 19,167 scintillation triplets from 1,391 closure-capable Parkes/PPTA epochs; 1,093 epochs form the independent sample. The broader 15-pulsar catalog includes PSR J1603-7202, ten Jiamusi pulsars, and three MeerKAT pulsars. While J0437-4715 provides the primary phase-domain rejection of the ψ=0 null, PSR J1603-7202 contributes complementary bipolar geometric structure from a distinct line of sight at different velocity geometry. The Jiamusi and MeerKAT samples are noise-limited because they contain only 1–2 closure-capable epochs; they provide bounds but do not independently diagnose environmental suppression.

J0437-4715 shows a non-zero Phase Closure signal. Because the Rayleigh and V-test statistics measure circular concentration against uniformity (and are rotation-invariant with respect to the mean angle), circular concentration and zero-mean rejection are reported separately: the unweighted circular mean is ψ=1.120 rad (95% bootstrap CI [+0.988,+1.254] rad excluding zero; circular concentration Rayleigh p=1.34×10⁻⁴⁴), and the weighted circular mean is ψ̄=0.984±0.046 rad with 95% circular-bootstrap confidence interval [0.737,1.235] rad excluding zero (>15σ circular mean offset from zero, corroborated in the delay domain by the MJD-ordered 15–240-epoch block-bootstrap noise-subtracted excess at 3.8σ–10.8σ, Steps 052 and 060; circular concentration R̄=0.308, Rayleigh p=1.39×10⁻¹³, V-test p=1.02×10⁻⁵ relative to μ_0 = 0). The unweighted statistic is identical in heliocentric and CMB-frame analyses, providing an implementation-invariance check; physical discrimination comes from the non-zero mean closure offset and its null controls.

PSR J1603-7202 has a 73.8° proper-motion separation from J0437-4715 and exhibits a frame-independent bipolar decomposition of the morphology expected for high-dispersion sightlines; its circular Phase Closure is noise-limited (R̄ = 0.019, Rayleigh p = 0.926), so the decomposition is a directional consistency check rather than demonstrated parity structure. Delay-domain unsigned amplitude estimators (M_cl) and their folded-normal Rice noise-floor bounds are documented in Appendix B.

Multiple independent checks support the phase-domain result. Phase-scramble and pre-alignment controls pass, unweighted ψ is strictly frame-invariant, signed-delay cancellation behaves as expected for a bipolar signal, and rigorous synthetic noise tests yielded zero false positives in 100 synthetic null trials. A signed-delay orbital diagnostic shows phase-locked structure directionally consistent with TEP kinematic coupling, though the hierarchical mixed-effects amplitude is not independently significant (p = 0.372, 2 df), as expected for a partially screened orbital channel. Multi-pulsar scaling, chromaticity, cross-telescope environmental bounds, and orbital structure provide multiscale consistency checks on the TEP framework.

The observation rejects the tested scalar-factorizable cross-term null. Within the TEP measurement model, the non-zero Phase Closure is a synchronization-holonomy candidate sourced by the non-exact disformal sector: on the measured screen-triangle geometry (Step 057), the canonical disformal connection yields ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹² s as a ceiling at order-unity drift inhomogeneity, with the B₀=+1 unit benchmark (1.3% of the narrowband-equivalent H_implied≈ 1.13×10⁻¹⁰ s on the median leg, 5.0% on the 95th-percentile leg) and reaches 1.14×10⁻¹⁰ s (100.5% on the median leg; B₀^req=20.1 on the p₉₅ leg) at the corpus's GW170817 galactic-profile envelope B₀≲ 77.7 (Paper 0, Step 50), while remaining within the delay-domain bound (≲ 0.46 ns). The tested scalar-factorizable implementations of thin-screen, multi-screen, refractive, chromatic-plasma and Doppler-delay models do not reproduce the observed coherent non-zero Phase Closure. The geometric structure from J1603-7202 is directionally consistent with the Temporal Equivalence Principle's non-integrable time transport.
